source: (cd lp-fw/fw-esp32c6 && cargo build --target riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf --profile release-esp32 --features esp32c6,test_rmt,ws281x_telemetry) && cargo run -q -p lp-emu-esp32c6 --release -- --elf target/riscv32imac-unknown-none-elf/release-esp32/fw-esp32c6 --time-grade t1 --usb-sj file:target/validate/rmt-chase.cap --usb-sj-tried file:target/validate/rmt-chase.tried --usb-host attached --dump-frames file:target/validate/rmt-chase.pins.jsonl --timeout 20s --wall-timeout 400 --strict-bus --exit-on '[rmt-chase] === DONE ===' --efuse-mac a0:f2:62:87:b4:8c --efuse-rev 0.2

trust.because: the allocator is the guest's own and the RAM model is byte-exact, and on the compile harness this configuration is byte-equal to silicon — 372/372 values, peak 48,132 / resident 18,932 / after-drop 3,976 B and all 184 per-tick figures (M3 P6). On the shipped image against the desk board, same commit and same bytes, the residual is EIGHT BYTES of `freeBytes` (complementary in `usedBytes`) and nothing else: `totalBytes` equal, the stack's first high-water mark equal to the byte on both the memfs pair (11,784 B, M6 P4) and the flash-backed pair (11,908 B, M6 P5). M3's 104 B was a sample of a live ~108 B allocation that comes and goes between heartbeats — silicon's own three read 266,392 / 266,496 / 266,388 — and §11.2's meteor `-4 B` is the same shape: one M6 P5 run reports both 152,316 and 152,320 five seconds apart. The eight bytes are not that: they repeat to the byte at 5 s and 10 s, across memfs and flash, across two commits, and across silicon boots 3 and 10, and the two machines agree to the byte on what the filesystem backing costs (1,296 B either side). One live 8-byte block silicon has and we do not, unnamed. Never tuned toward it

t1 counts one cycle per instruction — no cache, no flash wait states — and neither grade is graded by a transcript yet (the vision's 'time is a graded ladder, never a promise'). What is modelled honestly is the UART drain, at baud in emulated time, which is why the harness's log-bearing ticks land at 1.01x silicon while its compute ticks are 0.42x

there is no boot log: a direct load places the app's segments and jumps to its entry, so no ROM banner and no IDF bootloader lines are printed at all. M7 boots from reset and is where this class becomes a claim

M6 built the host's side — absent, attached with the port closed, attached and draining — and four committed transcripts under `lp-emu/transcripts/esp32c6/` are what it has to show for it: `boot-idle` over the shipped link against sitting 1's silicon capture of the SAME image bytes (stack high-water 11,784 B equal, heap 8 B apart); `usb-negative-control`, the port held closed from boot and opened at eight seconds, latching at 893 ms and recovering at 8,145; `usb-detach-reattach`, the cable out at six seconds and back at nine, recovering with exactly one hello and the firmware noticing nothing; and `usb-host-absent`, where the stamp pair reads 893 / never — the discriminator absent-vs-unread. The block's own registers are graded one by one (`--strict-grade`, the table in `periph/usb_sj.rs`) and the data path is `measured` there. M6 P5 adds the working half: the shipped image FROM FLASH over this link takes a real `lp-cli upload` (`upload-walk-usb`, `meteor-walk-usb`) with every filesystem write, every heap gate and every compiler output identical to M4's run of the same script over the spike's UART0 link — so the host model carries a day's work and not just a boot, and the link driver is demonstrably not in the heap ledger. This class stays `modeled` all the same, by the rule the ADR states and DD33 Q4 confirmed: byte-equality and agreement are EVIDENCE, weighed here where a reader can see them, not a promotion. The silicon transcript that would let anybody argue otherwise has now landed (`usb-negative-control/silicon-esp32c6-2026-09-07-b18360ea6.txt`, G3 step 4); whether it promotes this class is the director's to rule, not a phase's to assume

a pin IS observed (M5 P2): GPIO is a routing view over the bus's signal fabric, the RMT drives RMT_SIG_0/1 into it, and a WS281x decoder reads a routed pad's edges at the datasheet's +/-150 ns into frames (--dump-frames, --pin-log). Since M5 P3 a pin capture is COMMITTED beside the transcript (`rmt-chase`, 768 decoded frames of a 256-LED chase on gpio18) and the guest's own per-frame FNV-1a checksum agrees with the bytes the pad carried on every one of them, on both time grades. That is the strongest evidence this class has ever had and it is still not a measurement: both readings are ours. What would move the grade is a capture from an instrument on a real pin, and none exists. M5 P4 puts the first lit frame against the host oracle, which is the nearest independent check available without one

the bytes are the guest's own, drained through a UART0 model at the configured baud, so their content and order are the firmware's. What is not the firmware's is when a host's bytes arrive on a live socket — that is host time, not guest time, and `--uart0-script` is the deterministic path for anything a transcript should carry
